mechanism_narrative: The recent rise in WORKPLACES mobility and the simultaneous easing in TRANSIT and RETAIL_REC indicate a broad return-to-activity pattern that should continue to lift retail visits over the next four weeks as commuting and discretionary stopovers recover together.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not rise above the last 4-week mean, despite WORKPLACES remaining above t-3w levels and TRANSIT remaining less negative than t-3w for the next four weeks.

mechanism_narrative: When RESIDENTIAL mobility declines while GROCERy_PHARM stays elevated, people are spending more time outside home and converting nearby errands into broader shopping trips, which should raise RETAIL_REC within two weeks.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL falls below 4 points above baseline after having been above 5 points
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC fails to improve within two weeks after RESIDENTIAL drops below the stated threshold while GROCERY_PHARM remains positive.

mechanism_narrative: A renewed restriction regime that pushes TRANSIT and WORKPLACES farther below baseline will suppress discretionary shopping demand, causing RETAIL_REC to weaken over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT falls more than 5 points week-on-week and WORKPLACES falls more than 3 points week-on-week
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises or stays above its last 4-week mean after a simultaneous TRANSIT and WORKPLACES drop of the stated size.

mechanism_narrative: A seasonal holiday shopping effect operates when PARKS remain unusually negative and GROCERY_PHARM remains positive, because consumers substitute toward indoor shopping and errands, lifting RETAIL_REC over the next month.
candidate_trigger: PARKS stays below -15 points for two consecutive weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not exceed its prior 4-week average within four weeks of PARKS staying below -15 for two consecutive weeks.

mechanism_narrative: The persistent improvement in RETAIL_REC from t-3w to t-0w will continue because WORKPLACES and TRANSIT are still recovering from very depressed levels, so more people will combine work and shopping trips over the next week.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not post a higher weekly mean than t-0w in the next week even though WORKPLACES and TRANSIT remain below baseline.

mechanism_narrative: If GROCERY_PHARM continues rising while RESIDENTIAL stays positive, households are concentrating errands into local multi-purpose trips, which should spill over into higher RETAIL_REC within two weeks.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM rises above 6 points and RESIDENTIAL stays above 4 points
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC remains flat or declines over the next two weeks after GROCERY_PHARM rises above 6 and RESIDENTIAL stays above 4.

mechanism_narrative: When TRANSIT recovery stalls while WORKPLACES keep improving, office-linked retail demand decouples from commuting and retail mobility softens over the following four weeks.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT remains below -45 points for four consecutive weeks while WORKPLACES improve
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises above its last 4-week mean despite TRANSIT staying below -45 for four consecutive weeks and WORKPLACES improving.

mechanism_narrative: A short-lived year-end shopping burst emerges when PARKS rebound from a deep negative level, signaling indoor substitution away from outdoor leisure toward stores, which should lift RETAIL_REC over the next week.
candidate_trigger: PARKS improves by at least 4 points week-on-week after being below -18
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not increase in the next week after PARKS improves by at least 4 points from below -18.
